extracted.intended_audience: SEC staff, exchange members, market participants, and commenters reviewing the Exchange's fee/cost filing
extracted.subtask_description: Cost-allocation and cost-analysis methodology for an exchange's physical connectivity products (e.g., 10Gb ULL connections and Full Service MEO Ports), describing cost drivers, allocation steps, and calculations used to derive per-connection/port costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources cost driver
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Resources costs allocated based on employee time devoted to tasks related to providing physical connectivity (employee-by-employee allocation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate HR cost by consulting department leaders, determine which employees are involved in tasks related to providing physical connectivity, and confirm allocations are reasonable based on percentage of time devoted to those tasks. Use a blended rate of compensation reflecting salary, equity and bonus compensation, benefits, payroll taxes, and 401(k) matching contributions. For core networking teams the Exchange allocated a weighted average of 48.5% of each employee's time to 10Gb ULL connectivity; for ancillary personnel with a direct nexus (sales, finance, information security) applied a smaller allocation (less than 17%). Senior executives' time is allocated only to the extent they oversee tasks related to providing physical connectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivity (External Fees, Cabling, Switches, etc.) cost driver
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for external fees to connect to other exchanges and third parties and costs of cabling/switches required to operate the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cost driver is narrowly focused on technology needed to complete connections to the Exchange and to connect to external markets. The Exchange relies on third-party connectivity providers (including links to other national securities exchanges and OPRA); these services are critical for operations and are recouped in part via charges for 10Gb ULL connectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Services and External Market Data cost driver
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for internet, fiber, bandwidth connections across Exchange networks and fees paid to third parties to receive market data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include third-party providers that link primary/secondary data centers and offices. External market data fees are allocated to connectivity because market data is consumed at matching engine or port level to perform pre-trade risk checks and other validations (e.g., repricing to avoid locked/crossed markets, NBBO checks, halted-security checks). Allocation percentages may vary across affiliated markets due to technical architecture, market structure, business requirements, and differing port counts; allocations for this driver can be small when port counts are low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Center cost driver
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of leasing space and related services in third-party data centers (dedicated space, security, cooling, power) that house Exchange equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat data center costs as a direct cost of providing physical connectivity. The Exchange allocated a high percentage (61.8%) of the Data Center cost to physical 10Gb ULL connectivity because the third-party data centers and equipment contained therein are the most direct cost in providing physical access. Note the Exchange leases (does not own) its primary/secondary data centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardware and Software Maintenance and Licenses cost driver
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for hardware and software licenses used to operate, monitor, and support physical assets necessary to offer physical connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation reflects current hardware/software state and refresh timing; major hardware refreshes materially increase allocation. Example: MIAX Pearl Options allocated a higher percentage (59.8%) to 10Gb ULL connectivity due to an ongoing hardware refresh. For ports, include hardware/software used to monitor order-entry services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation cost driver
rubrics_metrics.description: Depreciation of physical assets, software and hardware used to provide connectivity, valued at cost and depreciated/leased over multi-year periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assets (including testing/monitoring equipment and in-house software when activated in production) are depreciated or leased over periods ranging from three to five years. Depreciation allocations should be narrowly tailored to connectivity-related assets; the Exchange allocated 61.3% of allocated depreciation costs to 10Gb ULL connectivity and 3.3% to Full Service MEO Ports. Differences across affiliates can be explained by asset age, system enhancements, and differing numbers of matching engines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocated Shared Expenses (general shared expenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Portion of general corporate/shared expenses (office occupancy/overhead, utilities, recruiting/training, marketing, professional fees, telecommunications, directors' fees, etc.) allocated to connectivity and then to sub-categories like 10Gb ULL connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a multi-layered allocation: first allocate general expenses among the Exchange and affiliated markets; then allocate the Exchange's share across core services (including connectivity); then allocate into sub-categories (e.g., 10Gb ULL). Determine percentages by looking at percentage allocations of each cost driver and holding meetings with senior management, department heads, and Finance to ensure proper and single allocation (no double-counting). Example: Exchange allocated 50.8% of the portion assigned to physical connectivity to 10Gb ULL connectivity and 3.0% to Full Service MEO Ports; rationale includes importance to strategy and product-specific weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-layered/two-step allocation process (affiliates then services/sub-categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-step allocation approach that first allocates costs among the Exchange and its affiliated markets and then allocates the Exchange's portion across core services and sub-categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: allocate among Exchange and affiliated markets based on factors like unique technical architecture, market structure, and business requirements. Step 2: allocate the portion assigned to the Exchange across core services (connectivity, ports, market data, etc.) and then into final product sub-categories (e.g., 10Gb ULL). This explains why percentage allocations differ across affiliates even when allocation methods are consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee-by-employee allocation and time-percentage basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, allocate costs on an employee-by-employee basis, including only personnel who support functions related to the product and applying an appropriate percentage of each employee's time to the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include departments predominantly involved (Business Systems Development, Trading Systems Development, Systems Operations and Network Monitoring, Network and Data Center Operations, Listings, Trading Operations, Project Management). Determine time percentages by consulting department leaders and confirming reasonableness. Example: network infrastructure personnel allocated 48.5% to 10Gb ULL and only 5.4% to Full Service MEO Ports; remaining time allocated to other services. Senior executives allocated only for oversight time.

rubrics_metrics.name: No full allocation and no double-counting principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange did not allocate any expenses in full to any core service and did not double-count any expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each expense is allocated proportionally across applicable core services and product groups so that no single cost is charged in full more than once. Apply the same Cost Analysis consistently across related filings (e.g., fee proposals for connectivity and proprietary data feeds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifiable-criteria allocation for per-connection/port costing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, allocate costs using quantifiable usage metrics (e.g., actual number of physical 10Gb connections or chargeable Full Service MEO Ports) to derive per-unit costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate approximate cost per connection/port by dividing total allocated monthly cost for the product by the number of chargeable units at the time pricing was determined. Example: total monthly cost for 10Gb ULL connectivity of $1,299,500 divided by 108 physical 10Gb ULL connections = approximately $12,032 per month per connection; Full Service MEO Ports: $165,793 monthly divided by 25 chargeable ports = approximately $6,632 per month per port.

rubrics_metrics.name: Port-specific allocation rationale (Full Service MEO Ports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate costs to Full Service MEO Ports based on the subset of resources and market data consumed at the port/order-entry level and relative port usage counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include HR (employees supporting ports), connectivity, internet services and external market data (a small allocation because market data is consumed at port level for order validation), data center, hardware/software maintenance, depreciation, and allocated shared expenses. Port allocations are sensitive to the number of ports utilized (fewer ports -> lower allocated percentage of some drivers). Example: for December 2023 the Exchange had 360 Full Service MEO Ports used across members versus larger counts on affiliates, resulting in lower allocation percentages for some drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness, documentation, and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Document and substantiate allocation percentages through consultation and governance: meetings with senior management, department heads, Finance Team, and analysis of usage/architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm allocations are reasonable by consulting department leaders to identify involved employees, documenting percentage of time devoted to tasks, and holding internal meetings to determine proper amounts. Use knowledge of technical architecture, recent initiatives (e.g., latency/determinism improvements), headcount changes, hardware refresh timing, and projected 2024 expenses to explain and justify allocation differences from prior years or affiliates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation/capitalization policy for in-house software and refreshes
rubrics_metrics.description: Software developed in-house is depreciated once activated in production; hardware/software costs from refreshes are capitalized and depreciated over defined periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for extended development (development + QA/testing) and amortize/depreciate capitalized improvements over the applicable useful life (3–5 years). Recognize that recent or planned refreshes increase depreciation expense and therefore allocation to connectivity/ports.
